title: Whose Transparency is it Anyway? Understanding Generative AI Transparency Needs and Gaps Across Stakeholders
abstract: arXiv:2611.05549v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Transparency has become a central principle in AI governance, yet there is little agreement about what transparency means, for whom, and in what contexts. Drawing on interpretive flexibility within the Social Construction of Technology, this paper examines how different stakeholders understand and experience transparency in generative AI. This study draws from a global survey of 400 end-users, AI builders, and policymakers, complemented by a structured focus group with end-users, grounding the quantitative findings in qualitative insights from the group most underserved by current transparency practice. We present three key findings. First, all three groups share similar understandings of what transparency means and what it should afford, centered on ensuring accuracy and privacy. translated_title: 这究竟是谁的透明度？理解生成式AI中不同利益相关者的透明度需求与差距
translated_abstract: 透明度已成为AI治理的核心原则，然而关于透明度究竟意味着什么、为谁服务以及在何种情境下适用，目前尚未达成共识。本文借助技术的社会建构理论中“解释灵活性”的概念，考察了不同利益相关者如何理解和体验生成式AI中的透明度。本研究基于一项覆盖400名最终用户、AI开发者和政策制定者的全球调查，并辅以针对最终用户的结构化焦点小组讨论，将定量发现扎根于当前透明度实践中服务最不足群体的定性洞察之上。我们提出了三个关键发现：第一，三个群体对透明度的含义及其应实现的功能有相似的理解，核心聚焦于确保准确性与隐私；第二，透明度特性的重要性与其实际可获得性之间的差距，在最终用户群体中远大于开发者群体，揭示了……
tldr: 本研究通过对最终用户、AI开发者和政策制定者的全球调查发现，尽管各方对透明度的理解相似，但最终用户在透明度需求与实际可获得性之间的差距远大于开发者，凸显了当前生成式AI透明度实践中的利益相关者不平等问题。
en_tdlr: Through a global survey of end-users, AI builders, and policymakers, this study reveals that despite shared understandings of transparency, end-users experience substantially larger gaps between the importance and availability of transparency features than builders, exposing inequities in current generative AI transparency practices.
